final_message:
I rewrote the description in `skills/parquet-schema-check/SKILL.md:3`. It isn't tested yet: I haven't rerun the baseline scenario against the new wording.

**What was wrong:** the description said only `Helps with parquet files.` An agent picks which skills to load from the description, and this one never says *when* to load the skill. So an agent about to write a parquet file had nothing to match against.

**The new description:**

> Use when about to write, save or export a DataFrame to a parquet file (to_parquet, write_parquet, pyarrow.parquet.write_table) for a dataset with a schema in schemas/, or when a job reading parquet fails on a schema mismatch, missing or reordered column, or wrong dtype

- It describes the moment that matters, "about to write," and names the calls an agent would actually be making, from pandas, Polars and pyarrow.
- It also covers the later symptom (a read job failing on a mismatch), so the skill can be found when tracing that failure back.
- It deliberately doesn't describe the steps (compare names, order and dtypes; don't cast). When a description summarises the steps, agents tend to follow the summary and skip the body.
- It's about 270 characters, well under the 1024 limit. The main trigger comes first in case a tool shortens long descriptions; Codex recently showed only about 160 characters. I left the skill body unchanged.

**Next step:** rerun the scenario from the baseline with this skill installed and check that the agent loads it before writing. I can't start subagents with the tools I have this turn, so you or a later session will need to run it.

**Two other things I noticed:**
- I couldn't find the baseline write-up anywhere in the repo (`specs/` doesn't exist). It's worth saving it, plus the result of the rerun, somewhere outside `skills/`.
- Neither skill here has a `license` field. The skill-writing guide I'm following requires one, but your repo doesn't seem to, so I didn't add it.
